From 08f5138512180a479ce6b9d23b825c9f4cd3be77 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Heiner Kallweit <hkallweit1@gmail.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Feb 2018 21:01:48 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] net: phy: fix phy_start to consider PHY_IGNORE_INTERRUPT

This condition wasn't adjusted when PHY_IGNORE_INTERRUPT (-2) was added
long ago. In case of PHY_IGNORE_INTERRUPT the MAC interrupt indicates
also PHY state changes and we should do what the symbol says.

Fixes: 84a527a41f38 ("net: phylib: fix interrupts re-enablement in phy_start")
Signed-off-by: Heiner Kallweit <hkallweit1@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Florian Fainelli <f.fainelli@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

diff --git a/drivers/net/phy/phy.c b/drivers/net/phy/phy.c
index f3313a129531..e3e29c2b028b 100644
--- a/drivers/net/phy/phy.c
+++ b/drivers/net/phy/phy.c
@@ -822,7 +822,7 @@ void phy_start(struct phy_device *phydev)
 		phy_resume(phydev);
 
 		/* make sure interrupts are re-enabled for the PHY */
-		if (phydev->irq != PHY_POLL) {
+		if (phy_interrupt_is_valid(phydev)) {
 			err = phy_enable_interrupts(phydev);
 			if (err < 0)
 				break;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/net/phy/phy.c`**
- The condition for checking if interrupts should be re-enabled in the `phy_start` function has been modified. 
- The original check `if (phydev->irq != PHY_POLL)` has been replaced with `if (phy_interrupt_is_valid(phydev))`. This change ensures that the function correctly considers the `PHY_IGNORE_INTERRUPT` state when determining if interrupts should be enabled.

### Relationships
- The modification addresses a previously unadjusted condition related to the handling of PHY interrupts, specifically in the context of the `PHY_IGNORE_INTERRUPT` constant. 
- This change is a direct fix to the bug introduced in a prior commit (identified by the hash `84a527a41f38`), which had not accounted for the implications of the `PHY_IGNORE_INTERRUPT` state when re-enabling interrupts in the `phy_start` function. The patch ensures that the behavior of the PHY state changes is correctly managed in accordance with the interrupt handling logic.
